Readback is limited (body must parse as SPARQL JSON; status text is echoed), hence medium.

message: CORS allows every origin, so any web page the user opens can call this server.
fix: Restrict Access-Control-Allow-Origin to known client origins, or keep it public but add rate limiting per origin/IP.
reason: The Cloudflare worker is a public, unauthenticated, read-only demo that uses no cookies or user credentials, so a wildcard CORS mostly lets other sites use the shared quota and its SSRF (see M001). Acceptable only if this instance is meant to be public.

title: server_url on every CKAN tool reaches internal hosts and the response body is echoed back
reason: server_url is attacker-controlled on every CKAN tool. The guard is a literal-hostname blocklist with no DNS resolution, and axios follows redirects without re-checking, so http://<name resolving to 169.254.169.254>/... or an external URL redirecting to an internal service is fetched; any non-CKAN response body is returned verbatim in the error text, giving full-read SSRF (e.g. cloud metadata credentials) when the server runs in Node/HTTP mode.
fix: In makeCkanRequest: resolve the host and reject private/loopback/link-local/unique-local results (use a custom lookup/agent so the checked IP is the one connected to), set maxRedirects: 0 or re-validate each redirect, and do not echo raw response bodies in errors.

title: Node HTTP transport listens on all interfaces with no authentication
reason: app.listen(port) without a host binds 0.0.0.0 and /mcp has no auth or Origin check, so anyone who can reach the port (or a web page via DNS rebinding) can drive the tools, including the SSRF in M001, from inside the server's network. Severity depends on where it is deployed.
fix: Bind to 127.0.0.1 by default (app.listen(port, '127.0.0.1')), validate Host/Origin headers, and require a bearer token when exposed beyond localhost.

title: Third-party portal content returned to the model unmarked
reason: Dataset titles/descriptions and raw responses from any portal the model is pointed at flow straight into the model context; a malicious portal can inject instructions (e.g. to call sparql_query/server_url with internal targets). Impact is bounded because all tools are read-only.
fix: Mark tool output as untrusted data and strip or truncate free-text fields from unknown portals.
